lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.note: Chapter heading.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.note: Chapter title. Leave a clean beat before story begins.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: By the time Zeek returned to the inn, the rain had begun.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: It tapped against the reed canopy stretched above the courtyard and ran in silver threads from its sagging edges. The basin beside the well had already overflowed, sending a narrow stream across the paving stones. Two carters sat beneath the driest corner, moving painted knucklebones through a game neither appeared to be winning.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Ninsun had covered the table with notes.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Copies of Ammaru's vanished entry lay beside her sketch of the impossible map. She had weighted each corner with a cup, a lamp, or one of BAH-lahg's knives. En-HEH-doo sat sideways on a stool, watching the courtyard entrance. BAH-lahg stood beside the wall with his arms crossed.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: All three looked at Zeek when he entered.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: BAH-lahg's gaze dropped to the satchel pressed against his ribs.

lines.speaker: Enhedu
lines.text: That is disappointing. I had hoped for someone competent.

lines.speaker: Zik
lines.text: He carried a message from the Collector.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The rain struck harder against the canopy.

lines.speaker: Zik
lines.text: He knows enough to offer ten times what he paid earlier.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Zik
lines.text: I was overcome by professional pride.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: En-HEH-doo leaned forward, forearms on her knees.

lines.speaker: Enhedu
lines.text: What else did the scribe say?

lines.speaker: Zik
lines.text: That we shouldn't return to the site.

lines.speaker: Balag
lines.text: For once, the Collector and I agree.

lines.speaker: Zik
lines.text: He also said the mark announces itself to people who have seen it before.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Ninsun's eyes dropped immediately to Zeek's hand.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The discoloration beneath his palm had faded until it resembled the shadow of an old scar. Zeek could still feel it pulsing. The sensation had not stopped since the answer beneath the city.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Ninsun
lines.text: But the Collector has seen it.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Zeek pulled his hand away before she touched him.

lines.speaker: Zik
lines.text: I am not going to scrape it.

lines.speaker: Ninsun
lines.text: That is exactly what a man says when he knows I intend to scrape something.

lines.speaker: Zik
lines.text: You may document it without removing any part of me.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: BAH-lahg pushed away from the wall.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Zeek placed the satchel on the table but kept one hand on it.

lines.speaker: Zik
lines.text: It became settled when the Collector told me not to go.

lines.speaker: Balag
lines.text: That is not how warnings work.

lines.speaker: Zik
lines.text: It is how his warnings work.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Ninsun drew her copied notes into a stack.

lines.speaker: Ninsun
lines.text: We return to the tomb, locate the seventh access, and determine whether the lower chambers correspond to the map.

lines.speaker: Balag
lines.text: You say that as though the map is a survey and not something drawn by a dead man's skin.

lines.speaker: Ninsun
lines.text: The material is irrelevant to the accuracy.

lines.speaker: Balag
lines.text: And at one point, presumably, opinions.

lines.speaker: Ninsun
lines.text: The opinions are irrelevant to the accuracy.

lines.speaker: Enhedu
lines.text: You are both assuming it wants us to reach the lower chamber.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Enhedu
lines.text: You intend to follow the road it drew.

lines.speaker: Zik
lines.text: I intend to reach the site before the Collector does.

lines.speaker: Enhedu
lines.text: You think he needs the map?

lines.speaker: Zik
lines.text: I think he may already know where it leads.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: BAH-lahg turned toward the courtyard entrance.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The musician who had been sitting beneath the awning was gone.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: His reed pipe remained beside the wall.

lines.speaker: Balag
lines.text: He was there when Zeek entered.

lines.speaker: Balag
lines.text: I did not see him leave.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The reed pipe lay where the musician had placed it, sheltered from the rain beneath a shallow niche. A few drops clung to its polished surface. The stool beside it was still angled toward the courtyard.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Zeek looked at the alley beyond the entrance.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: People moved past beneath cloaks and woven mats. A porter hurried after a donkey carrying twice its own width in bundled reeds. A woman held a clay bowl above her head as though the rain had chosen her personally.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Zeek had told himself the answer beneath Uruk might have been imagination.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The mark had burned. The journal had moved. The city had continued around him as though nothing had happened.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: He had almost believed that meant nothing had.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The journal shifted beneath his hand.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The cover lifted slightly against his palm.

lines.speaker: Ninsun
lines.text: It has already decided where it wants you.

lines.speaker: Zik
lines.text: That does not mean I have to obey.

lines.speaker: Zik
lines.text: I considered leaving it with my mother.

lines.speaker: Balag
lines.text: You took that thing into her house?

lines.speaker: Zik
lines.text: I did not open it near her.

lines.speaker: Balag
lines.text: That is a distinction only you would find reassuring.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The journal pushed against Zeek's hand again.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Something struck the inside of the cover.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The sound traveled through the table.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The carters near the well stopped their game.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: One of them looked toward Zeek's group, then quickly back at the knucklebones.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The journal struck the table twice.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Not from the wind. The air beneath the canopy was still.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: BAH-lahg placed his palm against the courtyard wall.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: En-HEH-doo crossed to him and touched the masonry with two fingers.

lines.speaker: Balag
lines.text: It was cold when we arrived,

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Rainwater struck the paving stones near its base.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: They trembled where they landed, then began to creep sideways.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Thin threads of water gathered between the stones and crawled toward the wall. One after another, they climbed into the mortar and vanished.

lines.speaker: Ninsun
lines.text: Water does not behave like that.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Enhedu
lines.text: I had been worried Uruk had changed its rules while we were inside.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The lantern flame leaned toward the masonry.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: BAH-lahg reached over his shoulder and drew his axe.

lines.speaker: Ninsun
lines.text: What exactly do you intend to strike?

lines.speaker: Balag
lines.text: The first thing that comes through.

lines.speaker: Ninsun
lines.text: That would be a poor archaeological decision.

lines.speaker: Balag
lines.text: It will be an excellent BAH-lahg decision.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: A tremor passed through the masonry.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The cups on the nearest table clicked together.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: One of the carters stood so quickly that his stool overturned. He muttered a prayer, swept the game pieces into his hand, and hurried toward the kitchen passage. His companion followed without asking whether the game was finished.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Zeek shoved the journal into the satchel.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Not enough to break. Enough to make the courses of brick appear soft beneath the lantern light.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Then it settled back into place.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Dark mortar lines spread across the surface.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: They climbed from the paving stones in two parallel columns before joining overhead, forming the outline of a tall, narrow doorway.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The proportions were wrong for an ordinary entrance. Too high. Too thin. Made for something that walked upright but had never learned the width of human shoulders.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The same shape as the shifted passages beneath the desert.

lines.speaker: Balag
lines.text: You can document it while moving.

lines.speaker: Ninsun
lines.text: A description made afterward will be less precise.

lines.speaker: Balag
lines.text: You will be less precise if the wall eats you.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: A black seam appeared between two courses of stone.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: It widened by the breadth of a fingernail.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The courtyard smelled suddenly of wet clay and something older—sealed dust, mineral oil, the breath of a chamber that had not opened in centuries.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Zeek slung the satchel over his shoulder.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: They crossed the courtyard as the seam widened behind them.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Ninsun walked backward, eyes fixed on the forming doorway.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: En-HEH-doo caught the back of Ninsun's robe and pulled her into the kitchen passage.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: They passed between steaming pots and hanging pans. The heat struck Zeek's face. A kitchen boy carrying a bowl of lentils twisted aside as BAH-lahg came through and slammed into a shelf instead.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: A bundle of onions dropped from its hook.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The cook turned from the hearth with a ladle raised like a weapon.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Something struck the courtyard wall behind them.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The cook looked toward the passage.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: They pushed through the crowded front room and into the street.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Wet evening air closed around them.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Merchants folded awnings beneath the rain. Donkeys crowded beneath overhangs and snapped at one another over dry ground. Two children splashed through the gutter while their mother shouted threats neither appeared to believe.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Behind the inn's shutters, stone struck stone again.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: A grinding impact that Zeek felt through the street beneath his sandals.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: A wine seller continued arguing over the price of a jar. A porter shoved past them with a basket balanced on his shoulders. A priest lifted his robe to avoid the gutter and stepped directly into a puddle.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Enhedu
lines.text: Uruk has high standards for public disturbances.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The satchel shifted against Zeek's hip.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: He pressed his arm against it.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Zik
lines.text: We take what we can carry, then leave through the drainage breach beneath the old lime kilns.

lines.speaker: Ninsun
lines.text: The east gate will be closed,

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Zik
lines.text: That is why we are not using it.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: BAH-lahg adjusted the axe on his shoulder.

lines.speaker: Balag
lines.text: You know a great many illegal exits.

lines.speaker: Zik
lines.text: I have been asked to leave several places without assistance.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Zeek kept them beneath the awnings where possible, though the rain had already darkened their robes. They crossed the potters' quarter, passed the shuttered stalls near the fish market, and turned west through lanes that narrowed as they approached the outer districts.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The journal did not knock again.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: That made Zeek trust it less.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Their rented room stood three districts away. By the time they reached the alley behind it, the rain had weakened to a fine mist.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The door appeared undisturbed. The upper shutter remained closed. No guards waited beneath the awnings. No temple scribes pretended to study wax tablets.

lines.speaker: Enhedu
lines.text: The shutter hook is turned inward.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: He could barely see it from the alley.

lines.speaker: Enhedu
lines.text: I put it the other way.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: They passed the entrance without slowing and entered the stable behind the adjoining house. A horse lifted its head as they crossed, considered objecting, then returned to its feed.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: BAH-lahg braced himself beneath the edge of the roof.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: En-HEH-doo stepped onto his clasped hands.

lines.speaker: Enhedu
lines.text: You could warn me before placing your entire weight on one finger.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: She caught the roofline, pulled herself up, and disappeared over the edge. A moment later a cord dropped beside BAH-lahg's face.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Zeek followed, then helped BAH-lahg haul himself onto the roof with considerably less grace than the horse below had shown.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: They crossed the wet tiles on hands and knees.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: En-HEH-doo reached the shutter, drew a narrow hook from her sleeve, and fed it through the gap. A soft scrape came from inside. The catch lifted.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: She opened the shutter by the width of a hand and listened.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: A moment later she leaned out.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: They entered one at a time.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The room looked exactly as they had left it.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: That was the first indication En-HEH-doo had been right.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The lamp sat in the center of the table. Their food remained stacked against the wall. BAYL-ID-din's field notes lay beneath a folded cloth. BAH-lahg's spare sandals still protruded from his pack at an angle that suggested they were trying to escape.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: A thin layer of dust covered the wood.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Someone had rested an arm across it.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The print was faint but clear: forearm, wrist, the edge of a hand.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Zeek checked the loose notes, clay impressions, tools, oil jars, and food.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Ninsun crouched beside the western wall.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The mortar around it had been cut and pressed back into place.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: BAH-lahg knelt beside her and worked the brick free with the tip of his knife.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: A strip of wet clay rested inside the cavity.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Four descending wedges had been marked on it.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Ninsun lifted the strip carefully between both hands.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The clay sagged slightly beneath its own weight.

lines.speaker: Ninsun
lines.text: The first three were made together,

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Ninsun
lines.text: The pressure is equal. Same tool, same angle.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: She turned it toward the vent.

lines.speaker: Ninsun
lines.text: Long enough for the surface to begin drying.

lines.speaker: Zik
lines.text: It means whoever entered wanted us to find it,

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Enhedu
lines.text: Then let us disappoint them by leaving.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: BAH-lahg laid the equipment across the floor and divided it into piles.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Two ropes. Four lamps. Spare oil. Wooden wedges. Bronze chisels. A hammer. Waterskins. Barley cakes. Dates. Bandages. Resin.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: He lifted the hammer, glanced at Zeek, and set it beside his own pack.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Ninsun added measuring cord, pigments, styluses, two clay tablets, and her copy of Ammaru's vanished ledger entry.

lines.speaker: Balag
lines.text: That will become important when you ask me to carry it.

lines.speaker: Balag
lines.text: You will place it beside my pack and stare.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: En-HEH-doo packed knives, wax, cord, two mirrors, a narrow saw, three hooks, and several tools Zeek could not identify.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Zeek lifted BAYL-ID-din's field notes from beneath the cloth.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Near the back, several pages had been folded inward.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: He had seen the creases before but assumed they marked damaged sections. Now he opened the first fold carefully.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: A plan of the tomb filled the page.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The burial chamber occupied the center, drawn in his father's precise hand. The entrance passage extended from one side. The shaft where KOO-rash had fallen was marked with a small cross.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Beneath the burial chamber, BAYL-ID-din had drawn another room.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Six chambers descended beneath the one they had entered.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Each was narrower than the level above it. Not stacked cleanly, but offset around a central vertical line, as though arranged along a buried spine.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: At the bottom of the page, BAYL-ID-din had written:

lines.speaker: Bel-iddin
lines.note: Bel-iddin's field notes.

lines.speaker: Ninsun
lines.text: He heard a void beneath the floor.

lines.speaker: Ninsun
lines.text: Or the same void at changing depths.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Ninsun took the page and held it nearer the vent.

lines.speaker: Ninsun
lines.text: These measurements were made at different points in the chamber.

lines.speaker: Ninsun
lines.text: The notation beside each count. North wall. Central slab. Eastern threshold.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Zeek remembered BAYL-ID-din walking the chamber with his head tilted, tapping the stone with the butt of a tool. At the time Zeek had assumed his father was looking for cracks.

lines.speaker: Bel-iddin
lines.text: Do not strike the black floor.
lines.note: Bel-iddin's field notes.

lines.speaker: Bel-iddin
lines.text: KOO-rash thinks it is stone. Do not let him test it.
lines.note: Bel-iddin's field notes.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: He remembered KOO-rash kneeling beside the smooth black surface, dust streaking his beard. He remembered the hammer rising.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: He remembered the sound that followed.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: BAH-lahg took the page from him.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: His eyes stopped at KOO-rash's name.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: BAH-lahg placed the page on the table.

lines.speaker: Balag
lines.text: You always find somewhere to move the blame.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Ninsun folded the warning page inward again, then changed her mind and carefully separated it from the binding where the stitching had already come loose.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Ninsun
lines.text: It says the one thing KOO-rash needed.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: A footstep sounded in the alley below.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Ninsun held the wet clay strip against her chest.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Zeek slipped one hand into the satchel and pressed his palm against the journal's cover.
